To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

femtosecond ablation of dielectric materials is governed by the balance of laser radiation absorption and its redistribution/redistribution in the bulk of the material, and the role of avalanche ionisation is negligible at the pulse durations of 100 fs and shorter.

the ablation thresholds are strongly influenced by air ionization and breakdown and, at high laser fluences (above the ablation threshold), the phase explosion is suppressed in the middle of the spot, where the laser energy absorption is the highest.
the ablation mechanism changes with the laser fluence, that the air plasma strongly affects the ablation rate, and that multi pulse ablation improves the crater quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of a novel method for the generation of high quality, large scale, ultrafast laser induced periodic surface structures on glass and transparent dielectric substrates.
the fundamental mechanisms of laser damage and white light emission upon irradiation of dielectrics.
fundamental aspects of laser ablation in wide bandgap materials, which is relevant for many applications in laser processing and material science.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanisms of ablation and light emission are complex and strongly depend on laser fluence and pulse number.
the mechanisms of the ablation and white light emission are strongly dependent on the laser pulse duration, the fluence, and the number of pulses.
the mechanisms of damage and white light emission in dielectrics are complex and strongly depend on laser parameters and the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanisms of damage and white light emission are not independent, and their interplay can be controlled by laser parameters.

the mechanisms of the ablation of wide bandgap materials by ultrashort pulses can be divided into two categories: (i) the mechanisms that are triggered by the laser pulse, and (ii) the mechanisms that occur after the laser pulse has passed and are triggered by plasma generated by the laser pulse.

the damage thresholds and the white light emission in glass can be controlled by the laser pulse parameters and the irradiation regime, which can be explained by the interplay between different ablation mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanisms of ablation of dielectric materials by ultrashort laser pulses are complex and can be influenced by the presence of plasma and its interaction with the laser pulse.
the damage thresholds are not universal and can be strongly affected by pulse energy density, number of pulses, and the laser pulse duration.
the ablation thresholds and mechanisms are strongly influenced by the laser parameters, especially by the pulse duration.
